workingTreeObservation.policy: Read Git objects at target, not owner moving edits; no project mutation.

conclusion: The public composer.cancel path and existing guard are appropriate for the proposed mounted material-await test. No new demonstrated blocking bug established in the fixed return path. A real uploaded requires-action attachment, observable adapter-send barrier and post-cancel late settlement are essential; HTTP ACK hold is a different downstream path.

facts.claim: Public cancel reaches the installed DefaultThread core; while preparing it aborts the submission and increments generation. A late adapter promise cannot dispatch the cancelled submission through _prepareSubmission.

Cancellation immediately returns A ahead of B in installed core; Flow restores the observed B text and removes only A ids absent from observed B. Returning-mask and private remove guard preserve held controller material; callback is guarded by active lifetime and exact captured object.

Public File upload yields requires-action and invokes adapter.send; choosing an existing complete file bypasses send altogether. Complete-file-only fixtures cannot prove the intended await/cancel branch.

Only actual local receipt handoff consumes material; failure/cancel retains it. Explicit complete-draft restore requires no B text/files or differently owned settings, pre-resolves held files, then rechecks ownership/generation/order around every attachment await.

mountedAcceptance.name: Prove the material barrier, not a network ACK pause
steps: Upload through the real official composer input until ready requires-action; optionally keep a preceding complete attachment to cover mixed ordered material.
Wait for fixture wrapper adapter.send entry AND public composer.submission plus preparing UI. Assert zero new turn/enqueue POST or local receipt before releasing that barrier.

Change next B via real UI (same text/different settings is discriminating; verify other pane unchanged), then fail or click the public preparation-cancel action. The wrapper must preserve original adapter and pass its options, not synthesize the prepared file or call onNew.
mountedAcceptance.why: All-complete branch dispatches synchronously; ACK pause is after onNew/receipt ownership and cannot exercise return guard.

mountedAcceptance.name: Cancel before late settlement; preserve B twice
steps: On cancel observe original signal.aborted and actual submission absence, then await returned/failed UI plus B preservation. Do not settle old promise first.

Release the original awaited adapter result only afterward (or reject it) and wait for an explicit wrapper-settled observation. Assert B text/settings/ordered material and opposite pane remain unchanged, old A not sent/enqueued, no additional send invocation.

A cooperative abort rejection alone is insufficient for late-success coverage. A narrow wrapper may defer the real result already obtained from the actual adapter; core generation protection is the target. No fake value or copied composer implementation.
mountedAcceptance.why: Installed AttachmentSendOperations caches a late real result without rechecking abort, but Base generation gate prevents dispatch; both observations distinguish harmless late resolution from B pollution.

mountedAcceptance.name: Exact ids/order, explicit restore and cleanup
steps: Before emptying B, click restore and verify a visible rejection with B wholly intact (settings-only B must also block). Then explicitly clear text/files and omit B settings, keeping intent/profile/knowledge consistent with held A.
Restore A once and assert exact old text, tuple and ordered unique attachment ids/references with no turn/enqueue POST. Repeated restore/normal observer notification must not duplicate chips.

After successful restore remove one complete chip via the real UI; its draft controller item disappears while held history/other material remains and no center-resource DELETE occurs. Ensure fixture barrier/listeners are disposed when its view/session ends.
mountedAcceptance.why: complete addAttachment appends without id dedup; Flow exact-id checks and held/restored bookkeeping, not core generic dedup, provide safety.

risksAndLimits.risk: Stale cancel click must not fall through to cancel-running-message semantics
risksAndLimits.recommendation: Render only preparing plus actual submission, subscribe to the public composer state, and recheck both immediately in the click handler. DefaultThread.cancel invokes the non-preparation cancel path if submission has already gone; when runtime supports running cancellation it may also delegate there. This is a proposed-UI guard, not a finding against unimplemented current cancel button.

risksAndLimits.risk: Same filename is not same attachment identity; no fabricated same-id injection
risksAndLimits.recommendation: Assert exact IDs/ref order through public UI. Existing-resource selection rejects duplicate resource references, complete addAttachment itself appends, and removeAttachment filters all matches by id. Do not claim global same-id safety from count/name-only checks, or manufacture otherwise unreachable duplicate IDs through page JS.

risksAndLimits.risk: Failure removing a returned A chip is an explicit incomplete return
risksAndLimits.recommendation: Do not hide the error or clear held A: bindPreparedDraftReturn keeps capture.returning when a remove rejects, so restore remains guarded. Existing direct tests cover basic failure/cancel and late restore; no mounted result or injected remove-rejection result is claimed by this review.

planAlignment: MSGAPP-03 requires freeze before material await and same-text/different-settings preservation; MSGAPP-04 complete-draft recovery; MSGAPP-05 real mounted browser remains required. Existing real-core direct tests are useful but do not establish mounted App/UI/HTTP behavior.

skills.application: Used installed local clean-code/webapp-testing references; no discovery network or install.
Traced one authority/lifetime, cancellation error path and concrete boundary tests; no framework or source changes.
Recommended waits for observable state transitions and real DOM/UI actions; no runtime/tools invoked.
